Draw an interactive pedigree diagram from a mating layout

Source: R/drawPedigreeDiagram.R
drawPedigreeDiagram.Rd

Returns an interactive pedigree diagram, as a visNetwork widget, for a layout made by makePedigreeMatingLayout. The diagram has the sex symbols at the layout's fixed positions, the legend (the five sex symbols, one row per affected condition or a single “Affected” row, a grey “Affected status unknown” row when an animal's status is unknown, a “Genotyped” row when an animal is genotyped, a “Carrier” row when an animal is a carrier, “Proband” and “Consultand” rows when an animal is one, an “Evaluated” row when an animal is evaluated, “Infertile” and “No offspring” rows when an animal is one, “Deceased”, and the dashed repeat-appearance and twin lines), each multi-condition symbol split into its colored sections, the slash through each deceased animal's symbol, a canvas that grows with the number of legend rows, the Export Diagram (PNG) button, a “Select by id” box that lists the animals, and the highlight on hover. The sections and the slash are painted by a drawing script inside the widget, so they appear wherever the widget is shown: in the RStudio viewer, in an R Markdown or Quarto document, or in a web page saved with htmlwidgets::saveWidget().

Usage

drawPedigreeDiagram(
  layout,
  edgeStyle = c("rectilinear", "direct"),
  onClick = NULL
)

Arguments

layout

the list returned by makePedigreeMatingLayout.

edgeStyle

the edgeStyle the layout was made with, "rectilinear" (the default) or "direct". It sets how far the hover highlight reaches: 6 steps under "rectilinear", whose invisible routing points count as steps, and 1 under "direct".

onClick

NULL (the default), or a JavaScript function, as a character string, that runs when the diagram is clicked. A Shiny application can pass one that sends the clicked animal to its server.

Value

A visNetwork widget, 500 pixels tall, 45 more for each affected condition past the first (at most four are drawn), for the “Affected status unknown” row, for the “Genotyped” row, for the “Carrier” row, for each of the “Proband” and “Consultand” rows, for the “Evaluated” row, for each of the “Infertile” and “No offspring” rows, and for each of the “Miscarriage”, “Termination” and “Ectopic” rows.

Details

With two or more conditions, every animal's symbol is cut into equal sections, one per condition, counter-clockwise from the top (the first of two is the left half), and each condition's legend row shows a circle cut the same way with that condition's section filled in its color, so the legend says which section is which.

The colours of the conditions are set by makePedigreeMatingLayout's conditionColors: the layout fills the symbols with them, and the drawing paints the sections and the legend's rows from the layout's conditions table, so all three agree.

An animal whose affected status is unknown (NA) is filled grey, with one condition, or has that condition's section grey, with two or more, so it does not look unaffected; the legend's grey hexagon “Affected status unknown” then says what the grey is, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for that row.

An animal whose genotyped column is TRUE (see makePedigreeMatingLayout) is drawn with its outline 4 pixels wide, where every other symbol's is 1 (at another lineWidth, that width plus 3 where every other symbol's is that width); the legend's “Genotyped” row, a square with that outline, then says what the thick outline is, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for that row.

An animal whose carrier column is TRUE (see makePedigreeMatingLayout) is drawn with a black dot at the centre of its symbol, on top of its fill, its sections and the slash; the legend's “Carrier” row, a circle with the dot, then says what the dot is, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for that row.

An animal whose proband or consultand column is TRUE (see makePedigreeMatingLayout) has a black arrow pointing at its symbol from the lower left, a proband's with “P” beside its tail; the legend's “Proband” and “Consultand” rows, each the arrow, then say what they are, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for each. The drawing takes in each arrow, so one at its left edge is not cut off.

An animal whose evaluated column is TRUE (see makePedigreeMatingLayout) has a black * to the right of the upper-right corner of its symbol; the legend's “Evaluated” row, the *, then says what it is, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for that row. The drawing takes in each *, so one at its right edge is not cut off.

An animal whose fertility column says it is infertile (see makePedigreeMatingLayout) has a black line down from the bottom of its symbol and two bars across it, and one with no offspring by choice or for an unknown reason a line and one bar, as in Pedixplorer; its id moves down below them. The legend's “Infertile” and “No offspring” rows, each its mark, then say what they are, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for each. The drawing takes in each moved id, so one in its bottom row is not cut off.

An animal whose miscarriage column says it is one (see makePedigreeMatingLayout) is drawn as a triangle 0.6 the size of the other symbols, so smaller than the “Unknown” sex's, with no deceased slash. The triangle of a termination of pregnancy or of an ectopic pregnancy has a black line across it from its lower-left to its upper-right corner, and an ectopic pregnancy's has “ECT” under it, as in Pedixplorer. Its id moves down into the row of the other ids. The legend's “Miscarriage”, “Termination” and “Ectopic” rows, each its triangle, then say what they are, and the canvas is 45 pixels taller for each. The drawing keeps the room a full-size symbol would have, so a long id at its edge is not cut off.

Each animal is drawn at the size makePedigreeMatingLayout's symbolSize gives it; an infertile animal's and a miscarriage's id moves down in proportion, and with symbols smaller than full size the drawing keeps the room a full-size symbol would have, so a long id at its edge is not cut off.

The ids and names are written at the size makePedigreeMatingLayout's textSize gives them; with text larger than before, the drawing keeps room for the outermost labels, so a long id at its edge is not cut off, and an infertile animal's and a miscarriage's moved id keep their room below their marks.

The lines are drawn at the width makePedigreeMatingLayout's lineWidth gives them, and each mark's lines (the deceased slash, the proband's arrow, the evaluated star, the infertile bars, the miscarriage line and the lines between the sections) that many times as wide as before; the legend keeps its widths, its “Genotyped” row among them.

A click does nothing unless onClick is given: a Shiny application can pass one to act on the clicked animal, which needs a live Shiny session, so a script leaves onClick out.

How large a drawing can be

On one Mac (Apple M2 Max), in November 2026, a synthetic colony of 1,000 animals took 16 seconds from findGeneration through makePedigreeMatingLayout and this function to a page drawn in Chrome, almost all of it in R, and one of 2,000 animals more than 120 seconds; with direct lines, 2,000 animals took 106 seconds. Judged by eye from those pages, a drawing can be read up to 1,000 animals, zoomed in. vignette("speed", package = "pedkindraw") gives these times, the times of the saved files and those of kinship2's and Pedixplorer's drawings.

See also

makePedigreeMatingLayout, savePedigreeDiagram to save the drawing as an SVG, a PDF or a PNG file, and runPedigreeApp, an app that draws a pedigree file with this function, with no code

Examples

## Four animals: A and B are the parents of C and D; A has died, and C
## is affected
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B"),
  sex = c("M", "F", "F", "M"),
  status = c("DECEASED", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE"),
  affected = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped)
diagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)
## Print `diagram` in an interactive session to see it, or save it as a web
## page with htmlwidgets::saveWidget(diagram, "pedigree.html").
